problem: The note says 'd=8 mm, stroke=3 mm'. In this chapter 3 mm is the effective stroke, not the total cam stroke, and Exam trap 1 warns students about exactly this mix-up. A reader can carry the wrong meaning away from the figure.
fix: Change the note to 'd = 8 mm, s_eff = 3 mm' (effective stroke, not total cam stroke).

problem: 'Pressure opens the delivery valve and the nozzle at its set pressure' can be read as if the delivery valve and the nozzle open at the same pressure. The delivery valve has only a light spring and opens well before the nozzle, which opens at its own set pressure (of the order of a few hundred bar).
fix: Write: 'Pressure opens the lightly spring-loaded delivery valve first; pressure then rises in the line and opens the nozzle needle at its set pressure.'

problem: 'check dynamic timing by spill or strobe method' mixes the two. Spill timing is normally a static, hand-turned check (delivery valve removed, fuel spills until the ports close); only the strobe/timing-light check is done with the engine running.
fix: Write: 'confirm port-closing (spill) timing statically by the spill method, then check running timing with a strobe on the flywheel marks.'

problem: The question asks for a comparison, but the answer covers only the pipe and pressure-lag side. For 5 marks a student also needs the other trade-offs: cam/rocker load and crowded head versus compact single-element layout, cost and service, and metering method.
fix: Add: 'The unit injector loads the engine camshaft and rocker and needs a crowded head with each unit set separately, so it costs more to buy and service; the distributor pump is compact, cheaper and has one element to calibrate, but its single plunger limits fuel and pressure and each cylinder needs its own pipe.'
